question.text: What determines whether a currency option is classified as European or American in India?

answer.text: In India, all exchange-traded currency options are European-style — this is mandated by exchange/SEBI rules and cannot be chosen by individual traders
The trader can choose European or American style when placing the order
USDINR options are American-style; cross-currency options are European
The exchange determines the style randomly for each contract

explanation.text: The Logic: In India, currency options in the ETCD segment — including USDINR and cross-currency pairs — are currently European-style under the contract/product specifications, and only European-style currency options are allowed in both OTC and exchange-traded segments at present. Traders therefore do not choose the exercise style. The Trap: The choices that suggest a trader-selectable style, or different styles for USDINR vs cross-currency options, contradict the product specifications which set all such contracts as European. Note: A European-style option can only be exercised at expiry; an American-style option can be exercised on any business day up to expiry. In India's currency segment, only the European style is permitted today.
